episodes.title: Uno
probes: Jimmy, scraping by on public defender work, tries hard to persuade a couple accused of embezzlement to retain him.

episodes.title: Mijo
probes: Out in the desert, Jimmy talks fast and nonstop at Tuco while the twins kneel in the dirt.
Jimmy keeps insisting, in a cheap suit and rising panic, that he is a lawyer, a public defender.
A soft-spoken young associate hands Jimmy a phone number, telling him to call when he's "in the game."

episodes.title: Nacho
probes: Jimmy notices a van parked near the Kettleman house with someone inside watching the place.
At a pay phone, Jimmy cups the receiver and puts on a strange, disguised voice.

episodes.title: Hero
probes: In a Cicero flashback, Jimmy and a buddy work a bar patron with a fake Rolex watch.
Jimmy puts up a billboard whose logo and clean-cut lawyer look are blatant copies of HHM's.

episodes.title: Alpine Shepherd Boy
probes: An elderly client dictates her will, leaving her collection of Hummel figurines to various friends and relatives.
Jimmy works the nursing home circuit dressed like the TV lawyer Matlock, in a pale suit.
The clients drawn in by Jimmy's recent local fame turn out to be far less promising than he hoped.

episodes.title: Five-O
probes: Jimmy, called in as Mike's lawyer at the police station, spills a full cup of coffee across the room.

episodes.title: Bingo
probes: Jimmy stacks boxes of legal documents in Chuck's house, hoping the cases will tempt his brother back to work.
Jimmy pitches Kim on the idea of the two of them going into a law partnership together.
Jimmy and Mike bring the borrowed notebook back to the two Philadelphia detectives, who are unimpressed by their explanation.
Jimmy arrives to find Chuck standing outside his house, insisting he is building up a tolerance to electromagnetic waves.

episodes.title: RICO
probes: Jimmy tells Chuck he studied law by distance learning through the University of American Samoa.
In a flashback, Jimmy is working in the HHM mailroom and celebrates wildly with Kim over his bar exam results.
Jimmy types up a hasty demand letter and hands it over at the retirement community's front office.

episodes.title: Pimento
probes: Sandpiper's lawyers bury Jimmy and Chuck under an avalanche of paperwork, boxes piling up around them.
Mike hires on as bodyguard for a jittery amateur who sells stolen pharmaceutical pills to Nacho.

episodes.title: Marco
probes: Jimmy is calling numbers at a bingo game in the senior center when he comes apart in front of the residents.
Back in Cicero, Jimmy sits in a bar with Marco, the two of them trading old stories.
Jimmy and Marco spend a solid week working one con after another around Cicero.

episodes.title: Switch
probes: In Omaha, Gene finds himself locked inside the mall's dumpster room, staring at an emergency exit he dares not push.
Someone scratches the letters "SG WAS HERE" into the wall before finally being let out of the locked room.
Daniel reports a burglary to the police, insisting the thieves took his valuable baseball card collection.

episodes.title: Cobbler
probes: Mike runs into Daniel outside the police station, where Daniel has come in for an interview about his stolen baseball cards.
Howard drives out to Chuck's house to tell him in person where Jimmy has taken a job.

episodes.title: Amarillo
probes: Jimmy pays off a Sandpiper shuttle driver so he can climb aboard and pitch himself to a busload of residents.
Mike stops by the veterinarian's clinic to look over what work is currently on offer.
Mike sits parked outside Stacey's house through the night, keeping watch on the quiet street.

episodes.title: Gloves Off
probes: Nacho, rattled by how unpredictable Tuco has become, worries his own side deals will come to light.
Jimmy sits in a conference room facing the Davis & Main partners, who are furious about the television commercial.

episodes.title: Rebecca
probes: Chuck attempts the same lighthearted routine his brother pulled off so easily, and it lands with a thud.
Kim works the phone through a long list of old school and professional contacts, hunting for a big client.
Jimmy finds Kim among the boxes in the document review room and floats the idea of suing the firm.
In a flashback soon after moving to Albuquerque, Jimmy charms Chuck's wife with easy patter while Chuck sits uncomfortably by.

episodes.title: Bali Ha'i
probes: Unable to sleep in his plush corporate apartment, Jimmy drives back to his old boiler room office and beds down there.
Kim, blowing off steam, works a bar con with Jimmy on an investor and keeps the resulting check as a souvenir.
Back at her old desk at HHM, Kim is handed menial busywork, including a hopeless motion to argue in court.

episodes.title: Inflatable
probes: In a flashback, a boy works the counter of his family's corner store while a stranger tells his father a hard-luck story.
Mike promises Stacey he will buy her a house in a safer neighborhood.

episodes.title: Fifi
probes: Jimmy talks his way onto an Air Force base and films a vintage bomber for a television ad.
Mike, parked and watching, tails a cargo truck out to an isolated garage on the edge of town.
Jimmy and Kim move their new offices into a converted dentists' suite, complete with leftover dental fittings.

episodes.title: Nailed
probes: Mike works alone in disguise on an empty desert road, going at a cargo truck's tire.
Jimmy loiters on the sidewalk across the street, keeping his eyes on a copy shop's front window.

episodes.title: Klick
probes: Jimmy slips out of their mother's hospital room to hunt down sandwiches, leaving Chuck sitting at the bedside.

episodes.title: Mabel
probes: Jimmy helps Chuck pull the foil sheeting off his walls, reminiscing about a children's book they once read together.
In black and white, a mall employee points out to security a shoplifter crouched inside a photo booth.
Mike methodically strips his station wagon down to its bare parts in a garage bay, checking every piece.

episodes.title: Witness
probes: Jimmy reports back to Mike that he noticed nothing unusual at all during his long stakeout over lunch.
Mike finds his missing gas cap sitting in the middle of an empty stretch of remote road.
Mike tails a courier's vehicle across town, staying several cars back through the traffic.

episodes.title: Sunk Costs
probes: On an empty desert road, Mike takes aim at a pair of sneakers strung over the overhead cable.
Mike watches a stretch of border road where drivers pull over and stash their guns before crossing.
Mike works a small packet of white powder down into the toe of a sneaker.

episodes.title: Sabrosito
probes: Mike turns up at Chuck's house in workman's clothes with a toolbox, replacing the damaged front door.
In a flashback, Hector arrives at the cartel boss's poolside estate carrying a cash tribute in a bag.
Jimmy, Kim, Howard and Chuck sit around a conference table with the prosecutor, going over paperwork together.
An envelope of cash arrives for Mike from Gus as payment, and Mike hands it back.

episodes.title: Chicanery
probes: In a flashback, Jimmy helps Chuck rig the house so Rebecca will not notice his condition over dinner.
At the bar association hearing, Kim frames the whole matter as a personal quarrel between two brothers.
Rebecca turns up in the hearing room just as Chuck arrives to give his testimony.

episodes.title: Off Brand
probes: Howard visits Chuck at home and urges him to let go of the feud with his brother.
Jimmy films quick, cheap TV spots for local businesses, trying not to waste commercial airtime he already paid for.

episodes.title: Expenses
probes: Mike turns up in work gloves to help build the church playground, joined by people from Stacey's support group.
Jimmy works the phones, trying to unload the television airtime he has already paid for.
At the support group, a woman tells the circle how her husband vanished on a hiking trip years ago.

episodes.title: Slip
probes: In a flashback, a young Jimmy and a friend dig out his old coin collection inside the shuttered family store in Cicero.
At lunch with Kevin and Paige, Kim spots Howard and tries to hand him a check for her law school loan.
On litter-collecting duty in an orange vest, Jimmy talks his community service supervisor into signing off on his hours.

episodes.title: Fall
probes: Jimmy presses Howard on why the firms won't take the settlement money now; Howard says patience will pay more.
Jimmy visits the elderly Sandpiper class representative at home, chatting with her for an update on the case.
Kim, juggling a second client on top of everything else, works herself to exhaustion at her desk.

episodes.title: Lantern
probes: In a childhood flashback, Chuck reads aloud to a young Jimmy by the light of a camping lantern.

episodes.title: Smoke
probes: A hospital clerk presses Gene for his personal information so she can complete the billing paperwork.
After his first Madrigal site visit, Mike hands over a detailed list of the safety violations he found.
Gene, riding in a taxi back to the mall, notices an Albuquerque Isotopes air freshener and gets out early.

episodes.title: Breathe
probes: Jimmy sits through a job interview at a copier showroom, pitching himself hard as a salesman.
Lydia is exasperated to learn Mike is actually walking Madrigal sites instead of just collecting paychecks.
Rebecca and Kim sit down in Howard's office to go through the paperwork of Chuck's estate.

episodes.title: Something Beautiful
probes: Kim is back at her desk on Mesa Verde business, uneasy about how fast the bank wants to expand.
Gus stops by a university chemistry lab to look over test results on meth samples he left there.
An after-hours job at the copier store nearly falls apart when it turns out the owner sleeps on the premises.

episodes.title: Talk
probes: Bored behind the counter of a nearly empty cell phone store, Jimmy tries to drum up business himself.
Kim sits at the back of a courtroom, watching a judge work through a day of small cases.
At the support group, Mike loses patience with another member's story about a wife who died.

episodes.title: Quite a Ride
probes: Kim, newly handed several pro bono defendants, stays with a courtroom case while Mesa Verde paperwork sits waiting.
Behind the counter, Jimmy talks a wary customer into buying several prepaid phones at once to protect his privacy.
In a flash-forward, Francesca hurriedly feeds documents into a shredder while Saul empties cash and mementos from his office.

episodes.title: Piñata
probes: In a flashback, Kim and Jimmy sort and deliver mail in the HHM mailroom, where she is still a law student.
At Hector's hospital bedside, Gus recounts a childhood story about a lúcuma tree he nursed back to health.
Mike quietly outfits hidden living quarters and recreation space underground for Werner's crew as they begin digging.

episodes.title: Something Stupid
probes: A long split-screen montage carries Jimmy and Kim through months of parallel daily routines as time slides forward.
Deep underground, the digging drags slower than expected, tempers fray, and Mike steps in to pull two workers apart.
Jimmy walks through empty office spaces, sizing them up for the practice he plans to reopen.

episodes.title: Coushatta
probes: Mike takes the German construction crew out to a strip club for a night off.
Kim rounds up staff at her new firm and promises to bury the prosecutor in paperwork.
On a long bus ride, Jimmy writes stacks of letters, switching pens, paper and handwriting, recruiting fellow passengers.

episodes.title: Wiedersehen
probes: Deep in the excavation, Werner's crew detonate the rock blocking the elevator shaft and cheer as the dust settles.
Jimmy sits before a panel, eloquently answering their questions about why he should have his law license back.
Lalo visits Hector's room carrying a small brass concierge bell he kept as a souvenir.

episodes.title: Winner
probes: Jimmy sits on the panel interviewing applicants for the scholarship established in Chuck's name, chatting with the candidates.
Lalo quietly watches Gus' operation from a distance, learning the routines and regular activities of the business.
In a flashback, Chuck puts on a show of celebration on the day Jimmy becomes a licensed attorney.
Kim organizes public occasions where Jimmy makes a visible display of mourning his brother in front of onlookers.

episodes.title: Magic Man
probes: Saul stands on a street corner handing out the last of his free cell phones to advertise his new practice.
Saul's camera crew films him staging a fake confrontation with a deputy district attorney as a publicity stunt.
Nacho passes along street rumors that the cocaine coming from Gus has been poor quality, and Lalo confirms it.
Jimmy tells Kim that the name he used for the phone business already comes with a ready-made client base.

episodes.title: 50% Off
probes: Saul contrives to be stuck in a courthouse elevator with the assistant district attorney, charm at full blast.
Two drug users flash one of Saul's 50% off business cards and embark on a multi-day binge.
At the Salamanca drug house, bags of product get jammed inside a drainpipe.

episodes.title: The Guy for This
probes: Kim is pulled away from a day of pro bono defense work to handle a homeowner refusing to sell his land.
Nacho quietly arranges for someone else to make an offer on his father's upholstery shop.
Jimmy, as Saul, stages an elaborate ploy designed to pull two DEA agents into his scheme.

episodes.title: Namaste
probes: A vanity plate reading "NAMAST3" sits on the back of an expensive car in a parking spot.
Jimmy picks out three bowling balls and hauls them off, though he never sets foot in a lane.

episodes.title: Dedicado a Max
probes: Mike recuperates in a small Mexican village, walking past a stone fountain with a dedication plaque on it.
A doctor patches up Mike's wounds and tells him he should stay put until he has healed.
Over another conversation, Howard presses Jimmy about the job offer, and Jimmy says he is still considering it.

episodes.title: Wexler v. Goodman
probes: Gus, Mike and Victor meet quietly with Nacho for an update on what Lalo has been planning.

episodes.title: JMM
probes: Gus sits with other subsidiary owners in a conference room, delivering business updates to Madrigal's visiting chief executive.
Away from the group, Gus quietly briefs Lydia and the Madrigal executive on where the lab construction stands.
Mike tells Stacey that he is past whatever had been making him so angry lately.

episodes.title: Bagman
probes: Jimmy drives out alone to a remote desert pickup site, where two heavy bags of cash are handed over.
Jimmy is paid a hundred thousand dollars up front for what he insists to Kim will be an easy job.

episodes.title: Bad Choice Road
probes: Mike tells Jimmy that the shakiness he feels after what happened in the desert will pass with time.

episodes.title: Something Unforgivable
probes: Kim takes on twenty pro bono cases at once from the public defender, hauling away the stack of files.
Howard suggests Kim stop following Jimmy's lead, and she tells him she's insulted by the idea she can't decide for herself.
Rather than staying at the apartment, Jimmy and Kim hole up in a downtown hotel room.

episodes.title: Wine and Roses
probes: Kim keeps watch on a leisurely round of golf while Jimmy slips unnoticed into the country club's locker room.
A long wordless sequence of a mansion being emptied, its white Cadillac rolled up onto a flatbed truck.
A souvenir tequila bottle stopper tumbles out of a cabinet as it is carried away with the furniture.

episodes.title: Carrot and Stick
probes: Jimmy turns up at a strip-mall tax preparation office run by a chirpy suburban husband and wife he knows.
Gus and Bolsa stand over Hector at the nursing home, promising him they will avenge Lalo.

episodes.title: Rock and Hard Place
probes: Jimmy and Kim toy with the idea of buying a duplicate of Howard's car before settling on something simpler.
Nacho, his shot-up truck no longer drivable, is left to hole up out of sight until daylight.
Jimmy and Kim enlist a pickpocket to lift Howard's car key long enough to copy it and the remote unlock button.
A prosecutor sits Kim down and asks her to get Jimmy to share what he knows about Lalo.

episodes.title: Hit and Run
probes: Evicted from the back room of the nail salon, Jimmy scouts out a potential new office and shows it to Kim.
Jimmy finds his fellow lawyers now cold toward him, while local criminals keep turning up wanting him to represent them.
Jimmy, done up to pass as Howard, drives Howard's car and picks up a woman from a motel.

episodes.title: Black and Blue
probes: Jimmy brings his old receptionist back on staff, hiring her to run the front desk again.
Kim keeps glancing over her shoulder, still unsettled by the possibility that Lalo is out there.

episodes.title: Axe and Grind
probes: A veterinarian shows Jimmy and Kim his thick encrypted notebook of criminal contacts, mentioning he is getting out of the business.
Cliff invites Kim to Santa Fe to meet foundation people who fund work like her pro bono defense practice.
A private investigator reports that the couple's days are dull and routine, apart from one recent cash withdrawal.

episodes.title: Point and Shoot
probes: Jimmy sits bound to a chair in his own living room while Lalo heads back out into the night.
Mike intercepts an unexpected late-night visitor at the front door of Gus' quiet suburban house.

episodes.title: Fun and Games
probes: Out of his usual uniform, Gus sits at a wine bar talking with his favourite sommelier, then leaves early.

episodes.title: Nippy
probes: In the department store, Gene lingers over a loud, garish shirt on the rack, then walks away without buying it.
In Omaha, Gene sets about befriending the elderly mother of the cab driver who recognized him, playing the helpful neighbor.

episodes.title: Breaking Bad
probes: At a set time, Gene uses a payphone to make a long-arranged call to Francesca.
Gene works a bar, buying rounds for a well-off man drinking alone until he is thoroughly drunk.
Jeff, driving a drunk passenger home, keeps offering him a bottle of water from the front seat.

episodes.title: Waterworks
probes: In a flashback, Kim runs into Jesse on the sidewalk outside Saul's office building.
Kim's days now consist of a drab office job at a Florida company that manufactures sprinklers.

episodes.title: Saul Gone
probes: In a flashback, Saul asks Mike what he most regrets; Mike answers, then dismisses Saul's own reply as shallow.
Saul and Walt trade answers about their biggest regrets while holed up together, and Walt scorns what Saul comes up with.
Jimmy cuts the conversation with his brother short, assuming the interest in his work is really criticism.
